items.literal_current_construction: For complete contact data, set $E:=(0,3/10]\cup[3/5,9/10]$ and take $Z_{A\sqcup B}=Z_{A\sqcup B}^{\mathrm{eq}}=\mathcal F$, with constituent maps $\xi_A,\xi_B$ the two coordinate projections and contact family $\mathcal T:=\{(c_A,x_A):x_A\in D_A\}\cup\{(c_B,x_B):x_B\in D_B\}$. The two constitutions share one species label. Give the aggregate constitution the domain $D_{A\sqcup B}=(0,\infty)^3$, and set $\xi_{A\sqcup B}(\phi(x))=(1,\hat V_A+\hat V_B,\hat n_A+\hat n_B)$. This is a supplied aggregate coordinate map for process records, not an assertion of an aggregate entropy identity. For each $x,y\in E$ with $y\ge x$, admit the record $P_{x,y}$ of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]] on $I=[0,1]$ seconds: its aggregate endpoints are both this constant coordinate tuple, $z_{x,y}(t)=\phi(x)$ for $0\le t<1$ and $z_{x,y}(1)=\phi(y)$, its control record is $(x,y)$, and its signed transfer record is the real number $x-y$. Declare the control-record set to be $\{(x,y)\in E^2:y\ge x\}$ and the transfer-record set to be $\mathbb R$. Each transfer record supplies $H_{P_{x,y}}^{\mathrm{in}},H_{P_{x,y}}^{\mathrm{out}}:[0,1]\to[0,\infty)$, both identically zero, with numerical values in joules; these maps are nondecreasing and start at zero. No path regularity is required by the supplier. The outer boundary admits no matter or energy transfer; fixed constituent volumes and amounts and zero contact work are retained constraints. Supply fixed positive constituent and compound masses and zero endpoint center-of-mass velocities in one Galilean chart, and no separately tracked external-field energy. Thus these are core closed records, with $Q[P_{x,y}]=W_{\mathrm{on}}[P_{x,y}]=0$. For the contact-record set $\mathcal P_T=\{P_{x,y}:x,y\in E,\ y\ge x\}$ supply $q_{A\to B}[P_{x,y}]=x-y$ in joule magnitudes as in [[def-td-thermal-contact-constraints]]. The constituent energy changes are $(y-x)\,\mathrm J$ and $(x-y)\,\mathrm J$. Each feasible endpoint has its self-record; nonzero transfers occur when $y>x$. No contact-equilibrium designation or relaxation law is assumed.
